The 'Tail' checkpoint was correctly marked untestable as it exits the frame. All other checkpoints were correctly identified as present. The Router missed that the low confidence in the hind limbs (from the pose auditor) correlates with the visual ambiguity of the rear body section, but since the tail is out of frame, this is likely occlusion rather than a structural defect.

Visually, the hindquarters fade into the rock/background with less definition than the forelimbs, suggesting minor fusion or 'melting' into the substrate. The topology mask shows a clean primary body but has small disconnected islands near the tail exit point, confirming slight boundary fragmentation. The severity of the limb fusion is underestimated by the Router; it affects the structural clarity of the pose. I am upgrading the artifact severity slightly to reflect the cumulative effect of limb ambiguity and background repetition.

The fine_grained_classifier confirmed the class with high confidence (logit 8.1). The only deduction is for the eye color nuance (amber vs golden) and the partial visibility of the tail, but these do not detract significantly from the overall class conformance.
artifact_reasoning: The image suffers from minor structural ambiguities. The animal_pose_auditor detected low confidence in the hind limbs, which visually corresponds to a lack of sharp definition where the rear legs meet the rock (minor fusion/melting). The background water exhibits repetitive, AI-typical wave patterns. While the foreground subject is largely coherent, the boundary integrity at the rear and the generic background texture prevent a higher artifact score. It is better than the 'mid' reference (hammerhead) which had significant blur, but worse than the 'high' reference (bird) which was sharp throughout.
